lines.text: Tech giants handed a random stranger over a hundred million dollars.
And they did it simply because he asked.
In twenty thirteen, Evaldas registered a fake electronics corporation in Latvia.
He picked the exact name of a real Asian hardware supplier.
Then he started mailing stacks of fake invoices to Google and Meta.
Inside corporate accounting, nobody even checked the bank account numbers.
Clerks casually stamped every multi-million dollar invoice as approved.
Wire transfers flooded his bank accounts across Cyprus, Latvia, and Hungary.
For two whole years, he bought luxury penthouses and sports cars.
Until a routine international wire transfer audit flagged the payments.
The feds seized seventy-five million, but were completely humiliated.
